% =====================================================================
\begin{abstract}
\noindent
The index of substitution saturation $\Iss=\Hbar/\HFSS$
\citep{xia2003iss} is used to decide, before any tree is built, whether an
alignment retains phylogenetic signal. We show that the entropy construction
enters $\E[\Iss]$ only through the spectrum of the rate matrix: resolving the
transition matrix on the eigenbasis of the symmetrised generator
$S=\Pi^{1/2}Q\Pi^{-1/2}$ reduces the index to a linear functional of the
coordinates $\xi_k=\langle e^{\lambda_k d}\rangle$, and $\Iss$ is an affine
function of the mean pairwise $p$-distance precisely when
$\tr A^{(k)}/\sum_j\pi_j A^{(k)}_{jj}$ is constant across the distinct non-zero
eigenvalues of $Q$. The criterion holds for every reversible model under
uniform base frequencies, and for every composition when the spectrum is
degenerate; in the F84 regime used to calibrate $\Iss$ it fails, though only to
first order in a composition term we quantify. Where it holds, $\Iss$ and the
mean $p$-distance induce the same ordering of alignments, so the content of the
test is carried entirely by the critical value --- and that value fails for
reasons independent of the spectrum. Being per-site, $\Iss$ is intensive, its
distribution invariant to sequence length to $O(L^{-1})$, whereas $\Issc$
increases with $L$; under $\Gamma$-distributed rates the tree length at which
$\Iss$ takes a given value depends strictly monotonically on the shape
parameter $\alpha$, a coordinate the published table does not contain. A
four-taxon transfer of long branches at fixed patristic total illustrates the
consequence: $\Iss$ is constant along the path to $O(r)$, while the probability
of recovering the true topology spans nearly its full range. Passing the test
is therefore strong evidence against saturation; failing it is weak evidence.
\end{abstract}

% =====================================================================
\section{Introduction}

The index of substitution saturation, $\Iss=\Hbar/\HFSS$, was introduced by
\citet{xia2003iss} to answer a question that substitution models address only
implicitly: have a set of sequences accumulated so many multiple substitutions
that their phylogenetic signal is exhausted? Its construction is deliberately
minimal. $\Hbar$ is the mean entropy of the base composition at a site,
$\HFSS$ the entropy expected under full saturation, so the ratio requires only
an alignment --- no tree, no model fit, no likelihood. That independence is why
it is used: $\Iss$ can be computed before any phylogeny is built, and compared
against a tabulated critical value $\Issc$ to decide in advance whether a data
set is fit for analysis \citep{xia2003iss,xia2009handbook}.

We show that the entropy construction enters $\E[\Iss]$ only through the
spectrum of the rate matrix, which makes the question of what $\Iss$ measures a
spectral one. Resolving the transition matrix on the eigenbasis of the
symmetrised generator $S=\Pi^{1/2}Q\Pi^{-1/2}$ reduces the index to a linear
functional of the coordinates $\xi_k=\langle e^{\lambda_k d}\rangle$, and the
affine relation to the mean pairwise $p$-distance follows precisely when
$\tr A^{(k)}/\sum_j\pi_j A^{(k)}_{jj}$ is constant across the distinct non-zero
eigenvalues of $Q$. The criterion holds for every reversible model under
uniform base frequencies and for every composition when the spectrum is
degenerate; in the F84 regime used to calibrate $\Iss$ it fails, though only to
first order in a composition term we quantify. Where it holds, $\Iss$ and mean
$p$-distance induce the same ordering of alignments, so the content of the test
is carried by the critical value --- and that value fails independently of the
spectrum. $\Iss$ is intensive, invariant to sequence length to $O(L^{-1})$,
whereas $\Issc$ grows with $L$; and under $\Gamma$-distributed rates the tree
length at which $\Iss$ takes a given value depends strictly monotonically on
the shape parameter $\alpha$, a coordinate the published table does not
contain. A four-taxon transfer of long branches at fixed patristic total
illustrates the consequence: $\Iss$ is constant along the path to $O(r)$, while
the probability of recovering the true topology spans nearly its full range.

\section{Setting and conventions}
\todo{fix the $H_{FSS}$ convention here; convention A (Xia Eq.~3) is primary}

Let $N$ sequences of length $L$ be related by a tree $\mathcal{T}$ with leaf
states generated by a reversible rate matrix $Q$ stationary with respect to
$\bpi$, normalised so that $-\sum_j\pi_jQ_{jj}=1$. Write $\hat{\mathbf p}^{(i)}$
for the empirical state frequencies at site $i$, $\hat p_j$ for their average
over sites (the pooled frequencies), and
\begin{equation}
  H_i=h(\hat{\mathbf p}^{(i)}),\qquad
  h(\mathbf p)=-\sum_j p_j\ln p_j,\qquad
  \Hbar=\frac1L\sum_{i=1}^{L}H_i .
\end{equation}
Xia's index is $\Iss=\Hbar/\HFSS$. The normalising constant admits two
readings, and we will need both:
\begin{equation}
  \HFSS^{(A)}=\E_{\mathbf n\sim\Mult(N,\hat{\mathbf p})}\bigl[h(\mathbf n/N)\bigr],
  \qquad
  \HFSS^{(B)}=h(\hat{\mathbf p}),
\end{equation}
convention $(A)$ being Xia's \citep{xia2003iss,xia2009handbook} and convention
$(B)$ the plug-in composition entropy. Since
$\HFSS^{(A)}=h(\hat{\mathbf p})-\frac{K-1}{2N}+O(N^{-2})$ with $K=4$ states, the
two are related pointwise on any data set by
\begin{equation}
  \Iss^{(A)}=c\,\Iss^{(B)},\qquad
  c=\frac{h(\hat{\mathbf p})}{\HFSS^{(A)}}\in(1,\,1.08]
  \ \text{for }N\ge 16 .
  \label{eq:convention}
\end{equation}
Convention therefore rescales the index but does not change which of two
alignments is more saturated, nor --- as we show in
Section~\ref{sec:criterion} --- whether the affine relation holds.

\section{Discussion}
\todo{Demarcation belongs here, stated as substance rather than as defence:
      \begin{itemize}
        \item \citet{verbruggen2007codium} and \citet{letsch2011rrna} question
              the threshold while accepting the index; we characterise the index.
        \item \citet{duchene2021saturation} operationalise saturation as long
              tree length, which is the same single-variable manipulation used
              to calibrate $\Iss$; a branch-level a posteriori test
              \citep{manuel2025satute} is a different object, and is what we
              take to be the right replacement.
        \item The bidirectional mis-calibration: omitting $\Gamma$ delays the
              decay of $\Pr[\hat{\mathcal T}=\mathcal T]$ (threshold too small),
              model misspecification accelerates it (threshold too large); the
              net sign is not determined.
      \end{itemize}}
